confirmed: Criterion 3 holds for all eight outcomes. Fluency is 'a count of the total number of ideas generated in the task by each respondent', and 'Raters recorded the fluency count and used the rubric to evaluate flexibility, originality and elaboration' on the submissions students made to the LMS. No outcome is a self-report (PDF p. 8, 'Measures and procedures').

AI availability: in the Experiment Group 'students were provided access to ChatGPT-3.5 and were specifically instructed to interact with the tool to assist in generating their ideas for the given task', and the scored submission came from that 15-minute task. The control group was told not to use generative AI. So ai_available_when_produced 'yes' and timing 'immediate' are right for all eight outcomes (PDF p. 7, 'Measures and procedures', and PDF p. 8 for the 15 minutes).
Question: no outcome measures diversity across people and no task ran after AI was removed, so 'with_ai' follows the codebook rule for all eight outcomes (codebook section 1, PDF p. 7-9).

Constructs: originality is 'uniqueness of ideas compared to what each rater saw in the overall sample', a rating of one student's submission, so novelty and not diversity. Elaboration is the 'degree of detail, specificity, and richness provided for ideas'. Flexibility is 'the variety of different categories of ideas produced' by one student, so flexibility. Fluency is the idea count (PDF p. 8, items (1) to (4)).

Measures: category_count fits fluency, because the raters counted the ideas by hand. expert_raters fits originality, elaboration, and flexibility: three raters scored them on a 5-point rubric, and 'the raters all had practical and theoretic experience of the three domains'. The same raters and rubric served both tasks, since they moderated six paperclip and six return-to-office submissions (PDF p. 8).

Unit: participant. Each measure is defined per respondent, and each rater scored every student's submission. Fluency, a per-student count, enters the same MANOVA as originality and elaboration, with group (and, for Entrepreneurship and Marketing, discipline) as the only factors. The error df, F(1,198) and F(1,120), fit about 202 and 122 rows (PDF p. 8-10).
Inter-rater correlations in measure_detail match the PDF: fluency .83-.95, flexibility > .75-.88, elaboration .60-.66, originality .32-.49 (PDF p. 8, last paragraph).

Flexibility was rated, and then 'the flexibility variable was dropped from the analysis' after a very strong correlation with fluency. So S1-O4 and S2-O4 rightly carry no contrasts (PDF p. 9, 'Data pre-processing').
All 18 cell means, their 18 unlabeled parentheticals, and the 9 significance values in the per-discipline and Management contrasts match Table 1 and Table 2 on the page image (PDF p. 10).

Every test statistic in the 'reported' fields matches the Results text. Multivariate: Pillai's trace = 0.06, F(3, 196) = 4.63, p = .004, partial η² = .06. Pooled univariate: F(1,198) = 0.14, 25.62, and 0.001. Interactions: F(1, 198) = 8.89, 3.80, and 17.23, partial η² = .04, .019, and .08. Management: Wilks Lambda = .07, F(3, 118) = 19.92, partial η² = .33, F(1,120) = 18.69, F(1,198) = 3.50, F(1, 120) = 41.34 (PDF p. 9-10).

Directions match the printed significance in all nine per-discipline and Management contrasts: Entrepreneurship .752, .817, .643 (no clear difference), Marketing <.001, .005, <.001 (treatment higher), Management <.001, .064, <.001 (higher, no clear difference, higher) (PDF p. 10, Tables 1-2 and the pairwise text below Table 2).

The form's cautions on the pooled S1 contrasts hold. With the parentheses read as standard errors, Table 1 implies discipline main effects of F = 0.15, 26.36, and 0.00 and intervention main effects of F = 6.07, 2.48, and 12.41 (fluency, originality, elaboration). The printed pooled 'intervention' F values (0.14, 25.62, 0.001) match the discipline effects, and the implied interactions (8.97, 3.93, 17.50) match the printed ones (my arithmetic on PDF p. 10, Table 1).

The form's Management checks hold. Partial η² = .03 for originality fits F = 3.50 with 120 error df (0.028), not 198 (0.017). Wilks Lambda = .07 would give F of about 523, while partial η² = .33 implies Lambda of about .67 and F of about 19.4, close to the printed 19.92 (PDF p. 10).

No outcome is missing. The paper scores only fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration. It has no similarity or diversity measure across students and no unassisted task after AI use. The overall three-discipline comparison appears only as 'Preliminary analyses did not reveal significant overarching trends beyond those observed within each discipline', with no numbers (PDF p. 9, Results).
PDF p. 12-16 hold the end of the Discussion, the Conclusion, a Note, Acknowledgements, Disclosure, ORCID, and References. There is no appendix or supplement with further outcomes (PDF p. 12-16).
summary: All eight outcomes (the fluency count and the rubric ratings of originality, elaboration, and flexibility) are scored by three domain-experienced raters on the ideas each student submitted in a 15-minute task, with ChatGPT-3.5 available to the experiment arm, so criterion 3 holds and with_ai, the constructs, the measures, the participant unit, and AI availability are all supported (PDF p. 7-9). Every number in the twelve contrasts matches Tables 1-2 and the Results text on the page images (PDF p. 9-10), no outcome that bears on the three questions is missing, and my arithmetic on Table 1 reproduces the form's caution that the printed pooled Entrepreneurship-plus-Marketing 'intervention' F values are probably the discipline effects.
